notes.1: The most common incorrect answer was A. Option A cannot true. For example, if element Y is sodium and element X is chlorine, the atomic radius of the elements decreases across period 3. Option B is correct because the lowest possible value for the atomic number of element Y is 1 and X is 7, so the n=1 shell of element X must be full.
notes.12: The most common incorrect answer was D. If the answer is D, then element E is chlorine. The 8th IE of chlorine is much greater than the 7th IE. The data in the question does not match this statement. Element E is silicon, which has four outer electrons in the 3rd shell. Once lost, the 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th electrons are all lost from the 2nd shell and would have comparable IE’s. The data in the question matches this statement, so the answer is A.
notes.13: The most common incorrect answer was B. The data in the question can be used to calculate that 0.070mol of Mg and 0.11mol of HCl is present. This means that HCl is the limiting reagent as 0.070mol of Mg would react with 0.14mol of HCl as per the balanced equation. In this reaction 0.055mol of H gas is produced. Under the conditions described in the question 0.055mol of gas occupies a volume of 1.3dm3 when given to two significant figures.
notes.22: The most common incorrect answer was A. ICl and Br have very similar instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces, as both molecules have 70 electrons, so the answer cannot be A or C. IBr does not have stronger permanent dipoles than ICl as Cl is more electronegative than Br, so the answer is B.
notes.28: The most common incorrect answer was B. Since the hydrocarbon is 14.3% H, it must be 85.7% C. Calculation shows the hydrocarbon has an empirical formula of CH . Since the hydrocarbon reacts with bromine by addition, it must be an alkene and have one C=C bond per molecule. This means one Br molecule reacts with one hydrocarbon molecule. Since 0.799g of Br contains 0.005mol, 0.280g of the hydrocarbon must also contain 0.005mol, so the M of the hydrocarbon is 56 and the molecular formula is C H . The answer is C and the four alkenes with this M are: • but-1-ene • cis but-2-ene • trans but-2-ene • methylpropene
notes.35: The most common incorrect answer was B. Most candidates knew that reaction 2 requires a reducing agent that will reduce a carbonyl group to an alcohol. Acidified sodium dichromate(VI) cannot be used for reaction 1 as it will oxidise the alcohol group to a ketone. This means that the correct answer is D.
notes.38: The most common incorrect answer was B. A and B can be ruled out since ester Z does not have one or more -O-C H groups. The best way to confirm that the X and Y given in C can react to form ester Z is to draw out the skeletal structure for Y. If the two -OH groups esterify with ethanoic acid, ester Z is produced.
notes.key_messages: Candidates who gave the best answers were concise and precise. The accurate use of chemical terminology remains crucial to remove ambiguity from responses. Candidates should be reminded to address ‘explain’ questions fully by stating facts or rules of thumb, and then showing how these combine to give reasons for chemical phenomena. This often requires a secure understanding of bonding and structure within molecules, in particular for organic species, linking structural feature to mechanistic probabilities.
